findings.title: Fallback ensure_loaded! runs on every request
findings.body: The new `I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` call in `set_locale` runs for every action via the `before_filter`. It allocates a new fallback array via `FallbackLocaleList#[]` on each call and then invokes `I18n.ensure_loaded!` for each entry, which performs an unsynchronized `Array#include?` against `@loaded_locales` inside the I18n translation path. For the common case where the user locale equals the default (and `:en` is already loaded), this allocates an array and does redundant checks on a hot path that runs for every request. Consider memoizing the resolved fallback list per locale or skipping the call when all entries are known to be loaded.

findings.title: New i18n fallback behavior added without any specs
findings.body: The PR introduces a new `FallbackLocaleList` class with custom `[]` and `ensure_loaded!` methods, deletes the standalone `pluralization.rb` initializer, replaces the default Rails fallback chain, and changes fallback semantics for every translated string on the server — yet no test files appear in the diff. This change deserves specs covering: fallback list contents and ordering for combinations of user locale / `SiteSetting.default_locale` / `:en`; deduplication when `locale` equals the default or is itself `:en`; `ensure_loaded!` idempotency; and that translations still resolve correctly through the custom list (including missing-key fallback to English).

findings.title: ensure_loaded! check is outside LOAD_MUTEX
findings.body: The newly added `ensure_loaded!` does `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` outside any mutex and then calls `load_locale`, which acquires `LOAD_MUTEX`. While `load_locale` re-checks `@loaded_locales.include?(locale)` under the mutex (so correctness is preserved), the outer include check is a TOCTOU pattern: multiple concurrent threads can race past it and redundantly contend on `LOAD_MUTEX`, doing duplicate Array scans and (in the worst case) holding the mutex while reading translation files. The `@loaded_locales ||= []` initialization is also unsynchronized (harmless here since both branches would assign empty arrays). Move the include check inside `LOAD_MUTEX.synchronize` (e.g., inline the load logic) to avoid wasted work under contention.

findings.title: FallbackLocaleList extends Hash unnecessarily
findings.body: `class FallbackLocaleList < Hash` inherits from Hash but the overridden `[]` never reads from Hash storage and no entries are ever written via `store=`/`[]=`. As a result, Hash methods such as `keys`, `values`, `each`, `empty?`, and `fetch` expose the empty underlying Hash state while `[]` returns a generated array — two contradictory views of the same object that will surprise future maintainers. The class also accepts only a single positional `locale`, whereas `I18n::Locale::Fallbacks#[]` accepts splat locales; if any plugin or i18n version ever passes multiple locales here it will raise `ArgumentError`. A plain class (or one whose `[]` takes `*locales`) would be both clearer and safer.
